title: FinOps for a lead: unit cost, showback and the bill nobody reads

videos.script: Coreto's cloud bill arrives every month, and every month it gets paid. {{title}} Nobody in engineering reads it. Yet every line on it is an engineering decision. A machine sized for a load nobody remembers. A test environment running all weekend. {{bill}} This lesson is about making that bill readable to the people who caused it. First, divide it by what the business sells. Next year the bill goes up eleven point three percent, and the cost of serving one ticket goes down twelve point two. Those are the same plan, read two ways. {{unit}} Then divide it by team, so each lead sees the part their own decisions made. Part of Coreto's bill has no owner at all, and you will share it out without hiding it. {{showback}} Last, the savings. They are rarely clever. The first one at Coreto was staging that nobody switched off at night, and it was worth nine thousand eight hundred reais a month. {{savings}}
